input.summary:
Implemented a complete in-memory Task Management API in TypeScript with the following files:

**src/event-bus.ts** — Generic pub/sub EventBus with typed `subscribe<T>` / `publish<T>` methods and safe mid-iteration unsubscription.

**src/types.ts** — All shared domain types (User, Project, Task, Comment, Notification) plus event payload interfaces and input types. Single source of truth for the data model.

**src/services/user-service.ts** — Full CRUD for users with email format validation and duplicate-email detection.

**src/services/project-service.ts** — Full CRUD for projects with addMember/removeMember operations; defers user-existence validation to the router.

**src/services/task-service.ts** — Full CRUD for tasks with enforced forward-only status transitions (todo → in-progress → done). Publishes `task.assigned` and `task.statusChanged` events via the EventBus.

**src/services/comment-service.ts** — CRUD for comments (filtered by taskId, sorted oldest-first). Publishes `comment.added` events; receives task context (title, assigneeId) from the router so it stays decoupled.

**src/services/notification-service.ts** — Subscribes to `task.assigned`, `task.statusChanged`, and `comment.added` events in its constructor. Creates notifications; skips self-notifications on comments. Exposes list (filtered by userId, newest-first) and markAsRead.

**src/router.ts** — Single HTTP entry point. Parses paths/query strings with zero external dependencies. Routes all 20+ endpoints to the correct service methods, handles cascade deletes (project→tasks, task→comments), and maps service errors to appropriate HTTP status codes (400/404/405).

**src/main.ts** — Composition root: wires all services through the EventBus, creates the ApiRouter, starts the HTTP server on port 3000.

**src/demo.ts** — Self-contained demo that spins up a server on port 3001 and exercises all features: user CRUD, project CRUD + membership, task creation/assignment/status transitions (including illegal transition rejection), comments, notifications (generation and mark-as-read), error handling, and cascade deletion. All 30+ assertions pass with green checkmarks.
